title: Fuel Access Diverged Across Russia’s Regions
subtitle: Refinery areas briefly improved, while delivery-dependent regions faced rationing, closures and farm shortages.

source.name: Regional fuel availability reporting, Reuters and Interfax

data.label: Omsk
data.detail: Purchase restrictions were removed in a major refinery region.

data.label: Volgograd
data.detail: Restrictions returned after another strike on the regional refinery.

data.label: Bashkortostan
data.detail: Repeated attacks tightened supply in and around the Ufa refining hub.

data.label: Astrakhan
data.detail: Many stations shortened operating hours to manage queues and shortages.

data.label: Kemerovo
data.detail: Around one third of stations in the region’s second-largest city were not operating.

data.label: Novosibirsk
data.detail: More than half of independent stations reportedly had no fuel.

data.label: Chelyabinsk
data.detail: Small farmers reported difficulty obtaining gasoline for field work.

data.label: Krasnodar
data.detail: Farmers received only half of their July fuel requirement and used reserves.

data.label: Bryansk
data.detail: Limits were 10 liters per customer, rising to 20 liters closer to the border.

data.label: Zabaykalsky
data.detail: Weekly deliveries were far below the monthly requirement.

supportingFacts.label: Detached-region limits were lifted, so it is retained as context rather than mapped.
Local refining capacity helped some regions recover only temporarily.

metadata.keyFinding: Fuel availability varied sharply by refinery access and delivery dependence.
